hero.title: Principal product designer, shaping how we connect
paragraphs: My career has taken me from games at Zynga to communication and AI at Google, and now AWS. The thread running through it is connection: sharing a world, keeping a conversation going, making complex systems easier to understand, and finding better ways to work together.

These days, I’m exploring what happens when AI becomes a teammate. That takes some imagining, and words only get us so far. I shape product direction and stay close to the craft, giving ideas a form my team can try, question, and build on together.

expertise.title: What I bring to the table

items.title: Product direction
items.description: I help teams work out what’s worth building, especially when the technology is new and the brief is still an argument. That means questioning assumptions, exploring alternatives, and giving people a direction they understand well enough to act on.

items.title: Interaction design & prototyping
items.description: Some ideas are hard to discuss until you can try them. I work through behavior, timing, and interaction details to give teams something concrete to question. A prototype tends to make the meeting more interesting.

items.title: Design leadership
items.description: I guide designers, work closely with engineering and research, and help leadership make decisions. I also work on the conditions around the design: who can decide, who needs to be involved, and whether anyone has actually spoken to a customer.

about.title: A little about me
paragraphs: Games and music have probably taught me as much about design as anything else. A game can teach you something difficult without making it feel like homework. A good instrument lets your hands catch up with an idea. I’m interested in how those things happen.
Outside of work, I make music and spend time with my wife and our three useless cats. The cats have contributed nothing to my career, but remain unusually confident in their qualifications.
